title: Minimax Inference for Recurrent-Event Contrasts When Censoring Retention Vanishes at the Endpoint
banked_reason: Fresh D0.5 typed panels pass with no findings, but the delivered independent Poisson/death benchmark grades subfield below field (6.8 < 7.4), not salvageable within scope; bank downgraded per supervisor and independent validity gate.
gap_reasons: The delivered results establish matching risk and honest-length orders within the smooth independent Poisson/death/censor benchmark, together with critical uniform studentization and fixed-law subcritical inference. They establish only converses over the endpoint-relaxed superclass, leaving its achievable precision unsettled. Exact constants remain open under sharp-limit-experiment; the framing does not claim that this question has been solved. The Rytgaard scope calculation nevertheless contains an incorrect equality: its observed-process intensity includes stopping at exit, so under continuous independent censoring the realized horizon product evaluates retention at that exit rather than equaling G_a(1)=0 almost surely; exclusion requires an essential-infimum argument ([equation 15](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2404.01736v4)). Known exponents and independent deterministic recurrence and death hazards restrict the contribution's applicability to substantive recurrent-event analyses. The projected score is constrained by that scope and by the absence of numerical evaluation showing whether the conservative envelope constants yield informative intervals at realistic sample sizes. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: The revived run retained only the supervisor-authorized continuation-bias proof-prose clarification, explicitly counting the band contribution once; no theorem statement or Lean source changed. Fresh D0.5 math and decision panels passed with no findings, clearing the prior overlap and first-order-bias objections. The general review nevertheless graded the restricted benchmark subfield below the field floor, with no bounded improvement directive; exact constants, broader-class attainment, and numerical calibration remain unresolved.
tldr: The randomized difference in expected recurrent counts remains identified when censor retention vanishes only at time one, but its estimation and inference change at \(\kappa=1\). The observable continued Kaplan--Meier/Nelson--Aalen estimator and full observed-history likelihood directions give matched squared-risk orders \(n^{-1}\), \(\log(n)/n\), and \(n^{-(2\beta+2)/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}\). Honest intervals have the corresponding optimal lengths, with a finite evaluable conservative constant computed from the declared class constants. For \(0<\kappa<1\), the ordinary estimator is root-\(n\) asymptotically linear despite zero horizon retention and has an observable consistent studentizer. At \(\kappa=1\), the continued estimator has a uniform studentized Gaussian law and explicit fallback. The smooth independent Poisson/death/censor model is a subclass benchmark; only the minimax and honest-length converses transfer automatically to the endpoint-relaxed superclass.
gap: Published causal recurrent-count procedures require treatment-times-censor retention bounded away from zero at the horizon; classical recurrent-mean procedures give regular inference rather than an endpoint frontier.
fill: The project combines an observable estimated-censor and estimated-death estimator, a full-history converse, matching honest length, critical studentization with an explicit full-range fallback, and an exact positive-retention reduction to the ordinary estimator.
